transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, I just can't seem to stop worrying. Once a thought starts—like about my mother getting up in the middle of the night, or a grant report I'm working on, or just wondering if I missed something at work—I just can't seem to put it away. I make lists, I try to focus on other things, but... it doesn't really help. I just can't shelve it.
Do these worries ever take the form of repetitive, intrusive thoughts that you try to suppress or ignore?

I don't... I'm not really sure what you mean by intrusive. They aren't strange thoughts or anything. They're just regular things, like I said. I don't really try to ignore them, I just... I just end up dwelling on them a lot.
Do you ever feel like you need to perform specific rituals or behaviors to reduce your worries or anxiety?
No... I don't think so. I don't do any rituals or anything like that. Just... just the lists I mentioned before.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of your worries?
No... not really. I still do everything I need to do. I don't avoid things.
Has something very stressful or traumatic happened to you recently or in the past?
No... nothing like that. Just... normal life, I suppose. Nothing traumatic.
Do you experience any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling when you're worrying?
No... I don't think so. I haven't really noticed anything like that. My heart doesn't race or... tremble. It's mostly just the worrying.
Do you find that your worrying affects your ability to concentrate or complete tasks?

I suppose... sometimes. Mostly at work. Like during cataloging reviews, or... staff meetings. I'll be looking right at the screen, or the agenda, and I just suddenly realize I haven't absorbed a single word. My mind just... wanders off into some problem I think I should have prevented. So... yes, it can be hard to focus.
How long have you been experiencing this excessive worrying?
I suppose... it's been a little over a year. Maybe a year and two months. It started around the time my mother had a fall... and she had to move in with me.
Has your worrying affected your relationships with family or friends?
I don't... I don't really think so. I tend to just keep things to myself, mostly. So... no, I haven't noticed any problems like that.
Did your mother's fall and subsequent move to live with you seem to trigger or coincide with the start of your worrying?

I suppose... I don't really know. It just sort of happened around the same time. I haven't really thought about it being a... trigger, or anything like that. It's just when things started getting worse, I guess.
Is your worrying generally about a wide range of things or is it mostly focused on one or two specific areas, like your mother or work?

I suppose... it's a lot of things now. It used to mostly just be about my mother's safety. But over this past year, it's... spread. 

I worry about finances, and... things at work, like staff decisions and deadlines. The house. Just... wondering whether I'm being a good daughter. It just feels like... even small things are about to unravel.
Have you noticed any changes in your social activities or hobbies since your worrying started?

Um... not really, no. I don't... I don't really go out much anyway. Between the library and taking care of my mother, there isn't a lot of extra time for hobbies. So... I haven't really noticed a difference.
Do you feel like your worrying is interfering with your overall well-being or quality of life?

I suppose... yes. It is. I... I've been making mistakes at work. Just small things, missing details at the library. But... it's not like me. And we had this grant presentation recently, and I just... I froze. I had to hand off parts of it to someone else. I just couldn't do it. It makes me wonder if I'm even... capable of leading my team anymore. So, yes... it's affecting things.
Do you find that you worry about things even when everything is going well and there are no obvious problems?
I don't know... I guess so. It just... it's always there in the background, even if things seem fine on the surface. I just... I can't really turn it off.
Do you worry about things at times when you are relaxed or doing something you enjoy?
Um... I'm not really sure. Like I said earlier, I don't... I don't really have much downtime to just relax. So... I couldn't really tell you.
Do you worry about your mother's safety when she is with you and you are confident that she is being well taken care of?
Um... no. Not really. If she's right there and... and I know she's fine, I don't think about it too much. So... no.
Do you find yourself worrying even when you're doing something you normally enjoy, like reading a book or watching a movie?
I mean... I don't really know. Like I said, I don't get a lot of time to just sit and read or... watch things. So I can't really say if I worry during those times.
Do you worry about things most of the day, nearly every day?

Um... I suppose so, yes. It's... it's kind of constant. 

Over the past year, it's... well, it's spread, I guess. It used to mostly just be about my mother's safety, but... now it's other things. Finances. Things at work, like... staff decisions and deadlines. The house. Just... worrying if I'm being a good daughter. 

It just feels like... I don't know, like even small things are about to unravel. So... yeah. Most days.
Do you feel like your worrying is making it hard for you to enjoy things or feel happy?
I... I don't really know. I don't spend a lot of time thinking about... being happy. I just sort of focus on getting through what needs to be done. So... I'm not sure.
Do you think your worrying is affecting your ability to enjoy time with your mother or take care of her the way you want to?

I... I don't know. I mean, I take care of her. That's just what I do. I make sure she has what she needs and that she's safe. I don't really... measure if I'm enjoying it or not. It's just my responsibility.
